verdicts.title: Public _addCredIdPerAddress/_removeCredIdPerAddress let anyone corrupt a holder's index and block full sells

a.reden: The candidate describes a public internal bookkeeping function vulnerability, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes missing access control on internal Cred bookkeeping helpers, which is unrelated to the known findings about signature replay, shareBalance bloating, reentrancy, or art settings

verdicts.title: Claims never check prior minting, so signatures/Merkle proofs can be replayed and quantity is unsigned

a.reden: The candidate describes missing mint‑state checks and unsigned quantity leading to replay, which differs from the chain‑id omission described in H‑01

b.reden: The candidate describes same-chain signature/Merkle replay due to missing nonce/used-state checks and unsigned quantity, not the known H-01 cross-chain replay caused by missing chain-id validation.

verdicts.title: buyShareCredFor / batchBuyShareCred reset victim's share lock, letting anyone block selling indefinitely

a.reden: The candidate describes a share lock reset issue, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a share-lock reset via buyShareCredFor/batchBuyShareCred, which is not the root cause of any listed known finding.

verdicts.title: getPositionsForCurator writes results at index i instead of the running index

a.reden: The candidate describes an out-of-bounds indexing bug in Cred.getPositionsForCurator, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes an array indexing bug in getPositionsForCurator, which is unrelated to any of the listed known findings.

verdicts.title: claim()/batchClaim() ignore msg.value and pay mint fees from the factory's own ETH balance

a.reden: The candidate describes a fee handling issue in claim/batchClaim, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes claim/batchClaim ignoring msg.value and using factory ETH, which is unrelated to any listed known finding.

verdicts.title: createArt signature does not cover CreateConfig and is replayable, so anyone can create arts and reset Merkle roots

a.reden: Both describe the same replayable signature flaw in createArt where CreateConfig isn’t included, enabling impersonation/royalty theft.

b.reden: Both findings describe the same root cause: createArt signature does not include CreateConfig parameters and is replayable, allowing unauthorized creation of art with arbitrary config.

verdicts.title: Refund goes to the NFT contract when claims use Claimable on PhiNFT1155, so excess ETH is stuck

a.reden: The candidate describes a refund handling issue in Claimable.sol causing ETH to be stuck, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes stuck ETH refunds sent to the NFT contract in Claimable, which is unrelated to the listed known findings.

verdicts.title: Curator rewards can be captured by just-in-time share purchase, atomically via buy-refund reentrancy

a.reden: The candidate describes a reentrancy issue in CuratorRewardsDistributor.distribute(), which is a different contract and function from the known reentrancy finding H-06 in Cred creation.

b.reden: Both exploit the same refund-before-state-update reentrancy in Cred's share-buy path to extract funds.

verdicts.title: Creator can change buy/sell royalty up to 50% at any time via updateCred, front-running holders

a.reden: The candidate describes a royalty change issue in Cred.updateCred, which does not correspond to any listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes a different vulnerability in Cred.sol's updateCred function, while none of the known findings address royalty changes in Cred.

verdicts.title: PhiNFT1155 caches protocolFeeDestination at init, so art-creation fees go to a stale address

a.reden: The candidate describes a stale fee destination caching issue, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes stale protocolFeeDestination caching in PhiNFT1155, which is unrelated to any listed known finding.

verdicts.title: createCred/updateCred signatures are replayable and not bound to chain or contract; royalties and creator_ are unsigned

a.reden: Different contract and function; root cause similar but not the same code location.

b.reden: The candidate describes signature replay in createCred/updateCred in Cred.sol, while known findings are about different functions in PhiFactory or other issues in Cred.

verdicts.title: Refund to msg.sender happens before lastTradeTimestamp is set, enabling lock bypass by reentrancy

a.reden: Both describe a reentrancy via refund before state update in Cred contract share purchase logic

b.reden: Both findings describe a reentrancy attack via the refund during buy, where the lock state is updated after the external call, allowing reentrance into sell functions.

verdicts.title: imageURI is unsigned and overwrites the minter's stored URI, so third parties can set it

a.reden: The candidate describes an unsigned imageURI overwrite bug, which does not correspond to any listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes an unsigned imageURI overwrite in PhiNFT1155.mint, which is a different root cause and contract than any known finding.

verdicts.title: Unbounded curator list (zero-balance entries never removed) can make distribute() run out of gas

a.reden: Both describe the same root cause of zero‑balance curator entries never being removed, leading to shareBalance bloating that can block/consume gas in reward distribution.

b.reden: Both describe the same root cause: zero-balance curator entries are never removed from shareBalance, causing unbounded growth and eventually blocking rewards distribution.

verdicts.title: TxOriginMismatch anti-contract check is bypassed by routing through claim()/batchClaim()

a.reden: The candidate describes a tx.origin check bypass, which is not covered by any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The known findings do not describe a tx.origin check bypass in claim/batchClaim.

verdicts.title: Fee setters treat mintProtocolFee and artCreateFee as basis points but they are used as flat wei amounts

a.reden: The candidate describes a fee misinterpretation bug, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate concerns fee setter unit/cap misconfiguration, which is unrelated to any listed known finding.

verdicts.title: createCred increments credIdCounter after external refund call; reentrancy corrupts cred IDs

a.reden: Both describe a reentrancy vulnerability in cred creation where a refund is sent before incrementing credIdCounter, allowing an attacker to corrupt IDs and steal funds.

b.reden: The candidate describes the same reentrancy in Cred creation via the ETH refund callback before state updates, matching H-06's root cause in the same function.

verdicts.title: Zero-balance holders are never removed from shareBalance map, so holder enumeration can be bloated to DoS distribute()

a.reden: Both describe zero-balance entries remaining in the EnumerableMap causing shareBalance bloating and DoS of curator reward distribution

b.reden: Both describe the same root cause: zero-balance curator entries remain in shareBalance, allowing enumeration bloating that DoSes rewards distribution.

verdicts.title: Claim signature's chainId field is not validated against block.chainid in signatureClaim

a.reden: Both describe the missing chain‑id validation in PhiFactory.signatureClaim allowing signature replay across chains

b.reden: Both describe missing chainId validation in signatureClaim allowing signature replay across chains.

verdicts.title: Royalty BPS is unbounded and royalties cannot be disabled

a.reden: The candidate describes an unbounded royalty BPS issue, which does not correspond to any of the listed known findings.

b.reden: The candidate describes unbounded royalty BPS and inability to disable royalties in CreatorRoyaltiesControl, which is a different root cause and code location from the known findings.

verdicts.title: buyShareCredFor lets anyone reset a victim's lastTradeTimestamp and keep their shares locked

a.reden: The candidate describes a timestamp reset vulnerability unrelated to any listed findings.

b.reden: No known finding describes the lastTradeTimestamp reset or forced share lock issue.

a.reden: The candidate describes a missing fee check and refund to a non-payable factory, which does not correspond to any listed known findings.
